claims.claim: Classes provide a means of bundling data and functionality together, creating a new type of object that allows new instances of that type to be made.
claims.quote: Classes provide a means of bundling data and functionality together.

claims.claim: Each class instance can have attributes attached to it for maintaining its state.
claims.quote: Each class instance can have attributes attached to it for maintaining its state.

claims.claim: When a class defines an __init__() method, class instantiation automatically invokes __init__() for the newly created class instance to establish its initial state.
claims.quote: When a class defines an __init__() method, class instantiation automatically invokes __init__() for the newly created class instance.

claims.claim: Often, the first argument of a method is called self, which represents the instance object.
claims.quote: Often, the first argument of a method is called self.

claims.claim: When you call a method, Python passes the instance object as the first argument of the function into self.
claims.quote: that the instance object is passed as the first argument of the function.

claims.claim: Inheritance allows a derived class to build on an existing class: writing class MinimalPublisher(Node) creates a class that inherits from Node so it already knows how to do everything a Node does.
claims.quote: Next, the ``MinimalPublisher`` class is created, which inherits from (or is a subclass of) `Node <{package_link(rclpy)}api/node.html>`__.

claims.claim: A callback is a function you hand to something else, which calls it later: you pass the function name without parentheses so it can be stored away and called at a later time.
claims.quote: However, it is not necessary to call a method right away: x.f is a method object, and can be stored away and called at a later time.

claims.claim: In the DrawCircleNode class below, the ROS 2 timer created with self.create_timer stands in for run_timer.
claims.quote: Next, `create_timer <{package_link(rclpy)}api/node.html#rclpy.node.Node.create_timer>`__ is used to create a callback that executes every 0.5 seconds.

claims.claim: The callback method self.send_velocity_command stands in for on_tick as the timer callback that ROS 2 executes.
claims.quote: First the {package(rclpy)} library is initialized, then the node is created, and then it "spins" the node (using `spin() <{package_link(rclpy)}api/init_shutdown.html#rclpy.spin>`__) so its callbacks are called.

claims.claim: The publisher stored on self.cmd_vel_pub_ stands in for the counter data so the node keeps its publisher available across timer callbacks.
claims.quote: ``self.i`` is a counter used in the callback.
